titleEn: How often should you be working at the office? Here’s what the research suggests
titleZh: 一周应到办公室几天？研究给出的建议
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: Office attendance from Monday to Friday used to be a pretty standard requirement for many jobs.
paragraphs.zh: 周一到周五的办公室出勤率曾经是许多工作的标准要求。

paragraphs.en: But plenty of employees have now developed a taste for working from home. And in response, some of their employers have started to tighten the rules on hybrid work.
paragraphs.zh: 但现在很多员工都喜欢在家工作。作为回应，他们的一些雇主已经开始收紧混合工作的规定。

paragraphs.en: Barclays Bank is one of latest big companies to do so, telling thousands of UK staff they must be in the office at least three days a week instead of two.
paragraphs.zh: 巴克莱银行（Barclays Bank）是最新一家这样做的大公司，它告诉数千名英国员工，他们必须每周至少在办公室工作三天，而不是两天。

paragraphs.en: So what is the right balance for those who split the locations of their working week?
paragraphs.zh: 那么，对于那些每周工作地点不同的人来说，什么是正确的平衡呢？

paragraphs.en: Plenty of research has now been done on that question. And while it does not give a single magic number, the evidence does suggest that the best range is two or three days in the office – on the same days as your colleagues.
paragraphs.zh: 关于这个问题，现在已经有了大量的研究。虽然它没有给出一个神奇的数字，但证据确实表明，最好的时间范围是在办公室呆两三天--和你的同事在同一天。

paragraphs.en: For example, in a study involving a large online travel agency in China, more than 1,500 engineers, marketing and finance staff were allowed to work from home on Wednesdays and Fridays, while a control group stayed in the office full time.
paragraphs.zh: 例如，在一项涉及中国一家大型在线旅行社的研究中，1,500多名工程师、营销和财务人员被允许在周三和周五在家工作，而对照组则全职呆在办公室。

paragraphs.en: Over the following two years of performance reviews, the performance of the hybrid workers was equal in quality to those who stayed in the office. And the ones who worked from home were much less likely to leave the company – especially women and the workers with long commutes.
paragraphs.zh: 在接下来两年的绩效评估中，混合型员工的表现在质量上与留在办公室的员工相当。在家工作的员工离开公司的可能性要小得多--尤其是女性和通勤时间较长的员工。

paragraphs.en: A smaller experiment at an international development organisation went a step further, by randomly varying how many days 148 staff spent in the office.
paragraphs.zh: 在一家国际发展组织进行的一项规模较小的实验更进一步，随机改变了148名员工在办公室的天数。

paragraphs.en: Those who came in around two days a week said they had a better work-life balance, more job satisfaction and less isolation than colleagues who came in more or less often. Their performance was unaffected.
paragraphs.zh: 那些每周来上班两天左右的人说，他们的工作与生活更平衡，工作满意度更高，比那些或多或少来上班的同事更少孤独。他们的表现没有受到影响。

paragraphs.en: These studies (among others) suggest that a week split roughly half and half between home and office costs employers little, while keeping staff happier and more likely to stay.
paragraphs.zh: 这些研究（以及其他研究）表明，一周在家和办公室之间的时间大致各占一半，这对雇主来说成本很低，同时让员工更快乐，更有可能留下来。

paragraphs.en: But there is also evidence that the office time counts, and that some work really does suffer at a distance.
paragraphs.zh: 但也有证据表明，办公时间很重要，有些工作确实会在远处受到影响。

paragraphs.en: In experiments across five countries, researchers found that video calls can reduce the flow of creative ideas. And an analysis of 20 million research papers and 4 million patents found that remote teams were less likely to produce breakthroughs. The evidence shows that being in the same room matters most when people are coming up with ideas together.
paragraphs.zh: 在五个国家的实验中，研究人员发现，视频通话会减少创意的交流。对2000万篇研究论文和400万项专利的分析发现，远程团队不太可能取得突破。证据表明，当人们一起想出创意时，在同一个房间里最重要。

paragraphs.en: But that doesn’t mean office workers should be together all day every day. In the Chinese travel agency trial, staff in the office three days a week did just as well as those in for five. The extra two days bought nothing measurable in performance – but more resignations.
paragraphs.zh: 但这并不意味着上班族应该每天都呆在一起。在中国旅行社的试验中，每周在办公室工作三天的员工和每周工作五天的员工表现一样好。多出来的两天在业绩上没有带来任何可衡量的结果，但辞职的人更多了。

paragraphs.en: Yet there is a risk that return-to-office rules set a minimum number of days with no maximum, so that the minimum number creeps up. A study of over 1,000 UK managers, found that employees working from home were less likely to be considered for promotion and pay rises. When being seen is rewarded “at least three days” can quietly become four or five days for those who want to climb the career ladder.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，有一种风险是，返回办公室的规定设定了最低天数，但没有设定最高天数，因此最低天数会慢慢增加。一项针对1,000多名英国经理的研究发现，在家工作的员工不太可能被考虑升职和加薪。对于那些希望在职业阶梯上攀登的人来说，被人看到的“至少三天”可能会悄悄变成四五天。

paragraphs.en: Together days
paragraphs.zh: 在一起的日子

paragraphs.en: How many days you spend in the office matters less if your colleagues are not there with you.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你的同事不在你身边，你在办公室呆多少天就不那么重要了。

paragraphs.en: A study of 48,000 employees at an IT firm found that during hybrid working, innovation suffered the most in teams where office attendance was poorly coordinated. This can mean that people commute in to work, find that their team members or close colleagues are not there, and then spend the day on video calls they could have joined from home. They experience the downsides of office working and get none of the benefit.
paragraphs.zh: 一项针对一家IT公司的4.8万名员工的研究发现，在混合工作模式下，办公室出勤率协调不佳的团队的创新能力受到的影响最大。这可能意味着，人们上下班时，会发现团队成员或亲密的同事不在，然后花一天的时间在视频电话上，他们本可以在家里加入。他们体验到了办公室工作的负面影响，却没有得到任何好处。

paragraphs.en: Overall then, the research so far on hybrid working suggests a few simple rules:
paragraphs.zh: 总的来说，迄今为止关于混合工作的研究提出了一些简单的规则：

paragraphs.en: The aim should be two or three days in the office, and that range should come with a maximum as well as a minimum.
paragraphs.zh: 目标应该是在办公室呆两到三天，这个范围应该有一个最大值和最小值。

paragraphs.en: Those days should be the same for for the whole team. The study of UK managers found that the career disadvantages that came with working from home disappeared in teams where it was the norm.
paragraphs.zh: 对于整个团队来说，这些日子应该都是一样的。对英国经理人的研究发现，在家工作带来的职业劣势在这种常态的团队中消失了。

paragraphs.en: Use office days for the things that benefit from being in the same room, like brainstorming or mentoring new staff. Keep home days for focused work.
paragraphs.zh: 把办公室的时间用来做那些在同一个房间里能受益的事情，比如头脑风暴或者指导新员工。把家庭的时间用来专注于工作。

paragraphs.en: No large study has yet directly compared two days in the office with three. But the overall picture is consistent. Two or three coordinated days seems to be the sweet spot, and employers who ask for more should be able to explain exactly what those extra days are for.
paragraphs.zh: 目前还没有一项大型研究直接比较两天和三天的工作时间。但总体情况是一致的。两天或三天协调工作似乎是最佳选择，要求延长工作时间的雇主应该能够准确解释这些额外的工作时间是为了什么。
